data.title: SEALSQ Posts Surging H1 2026 Revenue But Deeper Losses as Post-Quantum Investments Accelerate
data.description:
SEALSQ Corp ( (LAES) ) has shared an update.

On September 11, 2026, SEALSQ reported its financial and operational results for the six months ended June 30, 2026, highlighting sharp revenue growth alongside wider losses. Revenue rose 131% year-on-year to $11.2 million, gross profit jumped 233% to $5.4 million with margins near 48%, but operating loss widened to $32.2 million and net loss to $27.8 million as spending ramped.

Management attributed the top-line gains to renewed demand for Vault-IC secure elements, growth in PKI subscriptions and digital identity services, initial Quantix Edge Security revenue in Spain, and six months of IC’Alps consolidation. IC’Alps added about $2.5 million in sales and broadened the group’s custom ASIC design and secure semiconductor capabilities, while North America accounted for half of first-half revenue, underscoring the region’s importance.

The deeper losses reflected deliberate investment in post-quantum product development, certification, integration of acquired businesses and expansion of the SEALQUANTUM sovereign security stack. R&D nearly doubled to $8.7 million and general and administrative costs rose 68% to $23.1 million, partially offset by stronger gross profit and higher interest income on SEALSQ’s sizable liquidity reserves, which stood at $486.1 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash at mid-year.

Despite the negative earnings, the company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $27 million to $36 million and pointed to an active business pipeline exceeding $225 million through 2029, including more than $100 million tied to QS7001 and QVault TPM post-quantum projects. Certification milestones for the QS7001 chip, including NIST entropy-source validation and Common Criteria testing, and growing customer evaluations for QVault TPM suggest SEALSQ is positioning itself early in the emerging post-quantum security market, with substantial balance-sheet capacity to fund this strategy.

data.title: Eltel Wins EUR 73 Million KONSTANT Grid Contract, Boosts Danish Power Business
data.description:

The contract positions Eltel as a key partner in transformer station work, cable cabinet projects, maintenance and 24/7 monitoring, reinforcing its Power business in Jutland and prompting the recruitment of around 40 technicians as growing electrification and renewable adoption drive demand for more robust grids.

The agreement is strategically significant for Eltel, strengthening its foothold in the Danish power market at a time when heat pumps, electric vehicles, battery solutions, solar parks and other renewable energy sources are increasing the strain on distribution networks. By helping KONSTANT develop and operate a reliable electricity network, Eltel enhances its role in the Nordic energy transition and secures a long-term revenue stream in a market where grid resilience and modernization are becoming central concerns for utilities and infrastructure operators.

data.title: Cox de México Issues USD 800m Hybrid Bond to Cut Leverage and Support Investment Grade Ambitions
data.description:
An update from Cox Energy America SAB de CV Class A ( (MX:COXA) ) is now available.

Cox de México, via its subsidiary Cox Asset México, has placed a USD 800 million perpetual subordinated hybrid bond targeted at international institutional investors under the 144A/RegS format. Strong demand of more than USD 2.5 billion from about 125 investors across the U.S., the U.K., Europe, Asia and other regions underscored broad market confidence in the company’s credit profile.

The hybrid instrument carries an initial annual coupon of 8.75% and a first call date in September 2031, with proceeds primarily used to repay a USD 733 million term loan linked to the Iberdrola México acquisition. By replacing senior debt with equity-classified capital under IFRS, Cox Asset México cuts net leverage from 4.3x EBITDA to below 3.0x, reduces refinancing risk for roughly five years and strengthens its capital structure.

data.title: Balsu Bolsters Capital and Bets on Chile and Activated Carbon for Growth
data.description:

Balsu Gıda Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. has reinforced its balance sheet with a TRY 4.64 billion capital advance from its controlling shareholder, for which it has applied to convert into share capital through a private placement. This move would lift its equity-to-financial-debt ratio from 42.05% to around 74.47%, supporting financial resilience after a challenging hazelnut season marked by reduced crop, price volatility, weaker exports and a sharp rise in financing costs.

For the 2025/2026 financial year, the company reported consolidated revenue of TRY 22.62 billion, EBITDA of TRY 2.87 billion and net profit of TRY 254.3 million, as high raw material prices and extended inventory cycles weighed on margins. Looking ahead to 2026/2027, Balsu expects a more balanced hazelnut supply, stable revenue supported by higher volumes, faster cash conversion, significantly lower indebtedness and finance expenses, and a strong increase in net profit while preserving its EBITDA margin.

data.title: Hanking Gold Awards Metso Key Mt Bundy Crushing and Screening Contract
data.description:
China Hanking Holdings Ltd. ( (HK:3788) ) just unveiled an update.

Hanking Gold International’s Mt Bundy Gold Project has reached a key milestone with Primary Gold Pty Ltd awarding Metso Australia complete crushing and screening equipment packages for the dry plant, following a competitive tender managed by EPC contractor Delonix Solutions Projects. The scope covers HPGR, primary and secondary crushers, feeders and screens, and includes documentation plus commissioning and ramp-up support, forming the full dry circuit feeding the previously ordered wet plant ball mill.

The contracts were agreed on arm’s-length terms within the existing equipment budget, with progressive deliveries scheduled from March to June 2027, aligning with dry plant completion in late 2027 and first gold pour targeted for the first quarter of 2028. By choosing a single original equipment manufacturer for the entire crushing and screening circuit, the company expects clearer technical responsibility, faster and lower-risk ramp-up, and standardized maintenance and spares, which should reduce operational risk and support a smoother start-up for stakeholders in the Mt Bundy project.
